subject: Audit log handback, export formats & retention SLAs
messages:
From: David Owens <david.owens@acmeinc.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-ops@acmeinc.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Audit logs - export SLA, tamper-evidence and retention questions

Neha,

Thanks for the RFP materials you sent earlier this week. A few follow-ups from our security team as we map requirements for our procurement package (ACME RFI ID attached). Can you confirm the following items in writing so we can include them in our evaluation worksheet?

1) Export SLAs: If we request a bulk export (full audit stream) for an incident or compliance request, what is your guaranteed turnaround time? Is there an expedited option?

2) Export formats: Which machine-readable formats do you support natively for audit logs (event/time-series)? Are exports compressed/can you stream as ndjson/parquet?

3) Tamper evidence: Do exported bundles include checksums, immutable timestamps, and a chain-of-custody manifest? Any support for signed manifests (HMAC or PKI)?

4) Delivery & encryption: What delivery modes are available (S3 presigned, SFTP, direct transfer)? Do you support SSE-KMS and customer-managed keys for exported archives?

5) Retention windows & policies: What is the default retention for hosted logs vs Dedicated/Private deployments? Can retention be locked or set to legal hold?

6) Redaction & masking: Can exports be filtered or redacted pre-delivery? If so, what tooling / SLA applies?

We plan to include your responses in our Security appendix. If you can attach any spec docs or sample manifests that show the exported file layout and checksums, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a short, itemized response.

-David

Attachment: acme-rfi-attachment-ACME-1642.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: David Owens <david.owens@acmeinc.com>
Cc: security-ops@acmeinc.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI: Audit logs - export SLA, tamper-evidence and retention questions

David —

Thanks for the clear list. See answers below (concise) and attached sample spec + manifest. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through formats.

1) Export SLAs
- Standard: 72 hours from signed request for hosted accounts (includes validation and packaging).
- Expedited: 24 hours available as an add-on for Enterprise (requires pre-approved access window and notification to our ops team).
- For Dedicated/Private, we offer configurable on-prem tooling and can commit to tighter windows in the SOW.

2) Export formats
- Native supported formats: ndjson (newline-delimited JSON), Apache Parquet (columnar), and gzipped CSV for simple event tables.
- Exports can be split into time-sliced bundles (hour/day) to enable streaming download.
- We can also produce a compressed TAR of the bundle for single-download deliveries.

3) Tamper evidence
- Every export includes a manifest.json with per-file SHA256 checksums, a top-level bundle signature (HMAC-SHA256).
- Files are time-stamped with UTC ISO8601 event times and the bundle includes Redwood-issued provenance metadata (service version, compile id).
- For customers requesting PKI-signed manifests, we support signing manifests with customer-managed HSM keys in Dedicated/Private deployments (requires key provisioning in advance).

4) Delivery & encryption
- Delivery options: S3 presigned URLs (recommended), S3 push with SSE-KMS (customer or Redwood managed keys), SFTP, or direct TLS stream to a customer endpoint. For very large datasets we support AWS Snowball-type physical export (by exception).
- All transfers use TLS; at-rest encryption uses AES-256 with customer key options for Dedicated/Private.

5) Retention windows & policies
- Hosted default retention: 90 days for full audit stream; critical audit indexes retained 365 days depending on plan.
- Extended archival: optional cold storage up to 7 years (priced separately).
- Dedicated/Private: retention is configurable and can be set by policy and locked via support for legal hold/immutable retention windows (subject to contractual terms).

6) Redaction & masking
- Exports can be filtered by selector (time range, service, org-id) or run through server-side redaction rules prior to export.
- On-demand manual redaction (for PII) requires 48 hours prep for standard exports; expedited redaction is available as a professional services engagement.

Notes
- Cost: bulk export and expedited processing have associated fees; we provide an itemized fee schedule in the SOW.
- Evidence: attached "redwood-export-spec-20260918.pdf" and small "export-manifest-example.ndjson" showing manifest structure and checksum fields.

Next steps: please confirm the exact format you need (ndjson vs parquet), whether you will require KMS-managed keys, and whether expedited SLA should be included in the proposal.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Quick review from GTM/legal:
- We can offer the 24-hour expedited SLA as an Enterprise add-on. We should map it to a distinct line item in the proposal (ExpediteProcessingFee) and require a pre-negotiated maintenance window (to avoid mid-run operational risk).
- Egress & packaging fees: confirm we include a one-time packaging fee for very large exports (>5TB) and per-GB egress for hosted customers. Dedicated customers are typically priced differently in their contract.
- Legal redline: add a short clause for attestation of delivered bundle integrity and a certificate of deletion when the customer requests post-handoff destruction of the copies retained by Redwood (if applicable).

Markus: please confirm provisioning timeline for PKI signing (customer key import to our HSM / KMS) — I think 7-10 business days with standard onboarding; if correct, we will include that as a note in the SOW.

Once we have that confirmation I think we're ready to send the finalized response to Acme.
